What if I told you that one man was so clever… he actually managed to trick Death itself?
Not once. But twice!
His name was Sisyphus.
According to Greek mythology, Sisyphus was a cunning king who angered Zeus, the king of the gods.
So Zeus sent Thanatos, the god of Death, to take him to the underworld.
But Sisyphus had other plans.
He tricked Thanatos into putting on his own magical chains.
And suddenly… Death itself was trapped!
Nobody on Earth could die.
The gods were furious.
Eventually, Ares freed Thanatos, and Sisyphus was dragged into the underworld.
But somehow, he escaped again!
He convinced the rulers of the underworld to let him return to Earth to settle unfinished funeral rites.
Then he simply refused to come back.
For years, Sisyphus enjoyed the life he had stolen from Death.
But the gods finally caught him.
And here's the terrifying twist…
They didn't simply kill him.
Instead, they condemned him to push an enormous boulder up a mountain.
Every time he reached the top…
The boulder rolled all the way back down.
And he had to start again.
Forever.
He had cheated Death twice… only to receive a punishment that would never end.
